records.literal_gloss: And added [the] sons of Israel to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and gave them Yahweh into [the] hand of [the] Philistines forty years.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel again did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into [the] hand of the Philistines forty years.
en.B: Once more the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into the power of the Philistines for forty years.
en.R: Once more the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to the Philistines for forty years.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakaongeza kufanya maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mkononi mwa Wafilisti miaka arobaini.
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine Waisraeli walifanya yaliyo maovu machoni pa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia katika mamlaka ya Wafilisti kwa miaka arobaini.
sw.R: Kwa mara nyingine Waisraeli walifanya mambo ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema ni maovu. Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia mikononi mwa Wafilisti kwa miaka arobaini.

es.L: Y volvieron los hijos de Israel a hacer lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó en mano de los filisteos cuarenta años.
es.B: Una vez más los israelitas hicieron lo malo a los ojos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó en poder de los filisteos durante cuarenta años.
es.R: Una vez más los israelitas hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice que es malo. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó a los filisteos durante cuarenta años.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël continuèrent à faire le mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les livra dans la main des Philistins quarante ans.
fr.B: Une fois de plus, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent ce qui est mal aux yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les livra au pouvoir des Philistins pendant quarante ans.
fr.R: Une fois de plus, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déclare mal. Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les a livrés aux Philistins pendant quarante ans.

vi.L: Con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên lại làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phó họ vào tay người Phi-li-tin bốn mươi năm.
vi.B: Một lần nữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều ác trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phó họ vào quyền lực của người Phi-li-tin trong bốn mươi năm.
vi.R: Một lần nữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm điều mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} gọi là ác. Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giao họ cho người Phi-li-tin trong bốn mươi năm.

ko.L: 이스라엘 자손이 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 눈에 악한 일을 했다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 사십 년 동안 블레셋 사람들의 손에 넘겨주셨다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 자손이 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 보시기에 악한 일을 했다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 사십 년 동안 블레셋 사람들의 손에 넘겨주셨다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성이 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 악하다고 하신 일을 했다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 사십 년 동안 블레셋 사람들에게 넘기셨다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel voltaram a fazer o mal aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou na mão dos filisteus por quarenta anos.
pt.B: Mais uma vez os israelitas fizeram o que era mau aos olhos {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou ao poder dos filisteus durante quarenta anos.
pt.R: Mais uma vez os israelitas fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} considerava mau. Por isso {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os entregou aos filisteus durante quarenta anos.

decisions.choice: added to do: did again
decisions.reason: The verb "add" with another verb means doing something once more. The words open a new turn of the cycle of 2:11-19, as in 3:12, 4:1 and 10:6. Evil "in the eyes of" the LORD is evil as he judges it.

decisions.choice: gave them into the hand of the Philistines: put them under Philistine power
decisions.reason: "Hand" means power or control. The Philistines lived on the coastal plain to the west and pressed on Israel from there (10:7). Their rule here is the longest oppression in the book, forty years.

decisions.choice: no cry to the LORD is told
decisions.reason: In the earlier turns of the cycle Israel cries out to the LORD before he sends a rescuer (3:9, 15; 4:3; 6:6-7; 10:10). Here the story goes straight from the oppression to the birth of the rescuer. The LORD acts without being asked, and the rescue he begins through Samson is only a beginning (verse 5).

decisions.choice: gave them into the power of (Balanced); handed them over to (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the hand. Balanced and Readable say what it means, in the words used for the same formula in 6:1.

decisions.choice: "walifanya maovu machoni pa BWANA" (did evil in the eyes of the LORD); Readable "walifanya mambo ambayo BWANA alisema ni maovu"
decisions.reason: The refrain of Judges, worded as agreed for the book in every language: "machoni pa" keeps the Hebrew picture of the LORD's eyes at Literal and Balanced; Readable says plainly whose judgment it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "hicieron lo malo a los ojos del SEÑOR" (L, B); "hicieron lo que el SEÑOR dice que es malo" (R); "los filisteos"
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21, as the terms note sets: the book's refrain keeps the Hebrew "in the eyes of" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says plainly whose judgment it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "faire le mal aux yeux du SEIGNEUR" (L); "firent ce qui est mal aux yeux du SEIGNEUR" (B); "ont fait ce que le SEIGNEUR déclare mal" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books sets: Literal keeps the Hebrew article ("the evil") and the picture of the LORD's eyes; Balanced keeps the eyes in an idiom French readers know; Readable says plainly whose judgment it is, as the English Readable "did what the LORD said was evil".

decisions.choice: "주의 눈에 악한 일을 했다" (L), "주 보시기에 악한 일을 했다" (B), "주께서 악하다고 하신 일을 했다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verdict formula of the Kings terms note, so that this repeated line of Judges reads as it does through Kings. Readable says plainly that it is the LORD who calls the deeds evil, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "làm điều ác trước mặt CHÚA" (L, B); "làm điều mà CHÚA gọi là ác" (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain of Judges, as the Joshua–Ruth terms note sets it; Readable says whose judgement it is, as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: And there was one man from Zorah, from [the] clan of the Danites, and his name [was] Manoah; and his wife [was] barren and not she had borne.

en.L: And there was a certain man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, and his name [was] Manoah; and his wife [was] barren and had not borne [children].
en.B: There was a man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. His wife was unable to conceive and had borne no children.
en.R: There was a man named Manoah from the town of Zorah. He belonged to the clan of Dan. His wife could not have children, and she had never given birth.

sw.L: Na palikuwa na mtu mmoja wa Sora, wa ukoo wa Wadani, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Manoa; naye mkewe [alikuwa] tasa, wala hakuwa amezaa.
sw.B: Palikuwa na mtu mmoja wa Sora, wa ukoo wa Wadani, jina lake Manoa. Mkewe alikuwa tasa, hakuwa amezaa watoto.
sw.R: Palikuwa na mtu mmoja aitwaye Manoa kutoka mji wa Sora. Alikuwa wa ukoo wa Dani. Mke wake hakuweza kupata watoto, wala hakuwahi kuzaa.

es.L: Y había un hombre de Zora, del clan de los danitas, y su nombre [era] Manoa; y su mujer [era] estéril y no había dado a luz.
es.B: Había un hombre de Zora, del clan de los danitas, que se llamaba Manoa. Su esposa era estéril y no había tenido hijos.
es.R: Había un hombre llamado Manoa, del pueblo de Zora. Pertenecía al clan de Dan. Su esposa no podía tener hijos, y nunca había dado a luz.

fr.L: Et il y avait un homme de Tsorea, du clan des Danites, et son nom [était] Manoah ; et sa femme [était] stérile et n’avait pas enfanté.
fr.B: Il y avait un homme de Tsorea, du clan des Danites, qui s’appelait Manoah. Sa femme ne pouvait pas concevoir et n’avait pas eu d’enfants.
fr.R: Il y avait un homme appelé Manoah, de la ville de Tsorea. Il faisait partie du clan de Dan. Sa femme ne pouvait pas avoir d’enfants, et elle n’avait jamais accouché.

vi.L: Có một người ở Xô-ra, thuộc gia tộc người Đan, tên [là] Ma-nô-a; vợ ông son sẻ và chưa sinh [con].
vi.B: Có một người ở Xô-ra, thuộc gia tộc người Đan, tên là Ma-nô-a. Vợ ông hiếm muộn, không có con.
vi.R: Có một người tên là Ma-nô-a ở thành Xô-ra. Ông thuộc gia tộc Đan. Vợ ông không thể có con, và chưa từng sinh nở.

ko.L: 소라 출신으로 단 지파 가문에 속한 한 사람이 있었는데, 그의 이름은 마노아였다. 그의 아내는 임신하지 못하는 여자여서 [아이를] 낳지 못하였다.
ko.B: 소라 출신으로 단 지파 가문에 속한 마노아라는 사람이 있었다. 그의 아내는 임신하지 못하여 아이를 낳은 적이 없었다.
ko.R: 소라 성에 마노아라는 사람이 살았다. 그는 단 지파 가문 사람이었다. 그의 아내는 아이를 가질 수 없었고, 한 번도 아이를 낳아 본 적이 없었다.

pt.L: E havia um homem de Zorá, do clã dos danitas, e o seu nome [era] Manoá; e a sua mulher [era] estéril e não tinha dado à luz.
pt.B: Havia um homem de Zorá, do clã dos danitas, chamado Manoá. A sua mulher não podia engravidar e nunca tinha tido filhos.
pt.R: Havia um homem chamado Manoá, da cidade de Zorá. Ele era do clã de Dã. A sua mulher não podia ter filhos e nunca tinha ficado grávida.

decisions.choice: Zorah: a town in the low hills west of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Zorah lay on the edge of the hill country, looking down on the valley of Sorek and the Philistine plain. It was listed both for Judah (Joshua 15:33) and for Dan (Joshua 19:41). Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol (16:31), and the Danites set out from there to find new land (18:2, 8, 11).

decisions.choice: the clan of the Danites: the tribe of Dan, called a clan
decisions.reason: The word usually names a clan within a tribe, but here and in 18:2, 11, 19 it is used of Dan as a whole. Dan had not been able to hold the land given to it (1:34; 18:1), and part of the tribe was living in a small area around Zorah and Eshtaol.

decisions.choice: barren and had not borne children: she was childless
decisions.reason: Childlessness was a deep grief and often a shame for a wife. Scripture tells of several women who could not have children until God gave them a son who mattered for his people: Sarah (Genesis 11:30), Rebekah (Genesis 25:21), Rachel (Genesis 29:31) and Hannah (1 Samuel 1:2). Manoah's wife, whose name is never given, joins them.

decisions.choice: had not borne [children]
decisions.reason: The verb "bear" has no object in the Hebrew; Literal supplies one in brackets.

decisions.choice: the town of Zorah; the clan of Dan
decisions.reason: Readable says that Zorah is a town and gives the tribe's name instead of "the Danites".

decisions.choice: "Sora" for Zorah, "Wadani" for the Danites, "Manoa" for Manoah
decisions.reason: The names of the Samson story for this block: "Manoa" and "Samsoni" as agreed for Judges in every language (Samsoni as in Hebrews 11:32); "Sora" and "Eshtaoli" follow the Hebrew with the final vowel Swahili writes, and "Wadani" names the people of Dan as "Waisraeli" names Israel.

decisions.choice: "Manoa", "Zora", "Estaol", "Mahané-dan", "los danitas"; "Sansón" (verse 24)
decisions.reason: For Judges 13-16: the names in their usual Spanish forms; "Sansón" is the form Spanish already uses in Hebrews 11:32.

decisions.choice: "Tsorea", "Eshtaol", "les Danites", "Manoah"
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21: Zorah, Samson's home town (again in 13:25; 16:31; 18:2, 8, 11), is transcribed from the Hebrew with "ts" for tsade, as the Pentateuch's French names are; Manoah keeps the form the terms note for these books gives. Literal keeps "[était] stérile et n'avait pas enfanté"; French needs no bracketed "children" after "enfanté".

decisions.choice: "Xô-ra" for Zorah, "Ma-nô-a" for Manoah
decisions.reason: Manoah follows the Joshua–Ruth terms note; Zorah, first named in this block here, takes the usual Protestant spelling and keeps it through Samson's story.

decisions.choice: Manoá; Zorá; os danitas
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Samson's father takes the Brazilian form "Manoá", with the stress on the last syllable marked; the town keeps the form "Zorá" of Joshua 19:41 in Portuguese, and "danitas" that of Joshua 19:47. Samson's mother has no name in the text, and Portuguese calls her "a mulher" or "a sua mulher", as the Hebrew does.

records.literal_gloss: And appeared [the] angel of Yahweh to the woman and said to her, see now, you [are] barren and not you have borne; and you will conceive and bear [a] son.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to the woman and said to her, "See now, you [are] barren and have not borne [children]; but you will conceive and bear a son.
en.B: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to the woman. "Listen," he told her, "you are unable to conceive and have borne no children, but you will conceive and bear a son.
en.R: The angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to the woman. He said to her, "You have not been able to have children. But you will become pregnant and have a son.

es.B: El ángel {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se le apareció a la mujer y le dijo: «Escucha: tú eres estéril y no has tenido hijos, pero vas a concebir y darás a luz un hijo.

fr.L: Et l’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} apparut à la femme et lui dit : « Voici donc, tu [es] stérile et tu n’as pas enfanté ; mais tu concevras et tu enfanteras un fils.
fr.B: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} apparut à la femme. « Écoute, lui dit-il, tu ne peux pas concevoir et tu n’as pas eu d’enfants, mais tu vas concevoir et mettre au monde un fils.
fr.R: L’ange {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est apparu à la femme. Il lui a dit : « Tu n’as pas pu avoir d’enfants. Mais tu vas être enceinte et tu auras un fils.

vi.L: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với người đàn bà và nói với bà: "Này, bà son sẻ và chưa sinh [con]; nhưng bà sẽ thụ thai và sinh một con trai.
vi.B: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với người đàn bà và nói: "Này bà, bà hiếm muộn, chưa có con, nhưng bà sẽ thụ thai và sinh một con trai.
vi.R: Thiên sứ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với người đàn bà. Thiên sứ nói với bà: "Bà chưa thể có con. Nhưng bà sẽ có thai và sinh một con trai.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 그 여자에게 나타나 그에게 말했다. "보아라, 너는 임신하지 못하여 [아이를] 낳지 못하였으나, 임신하여 아들을 낳을 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 그 여자에게 나타나 말했다. "들어라. 너는 임신하지 못하여 아이를 낳지 못했다. 그러나 이제 임신하여 아들을 낳을 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 천사가 그 여자에게 나타났다. 천사가 그에게 말했다. "너는 아이를 가질 수 없었다. 그러나 이제 아이를 가져서 아들을 낳을 것이다.

pt.L: E o anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} apareceu à mulher e lhe disse: "Eis que tu [és] estéril e não deste à luz; mas conceberás e darás à luz um filho.
pt.B: O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} apareceu à mulher. "Escuta", disse-lhe ele, "tu não podes engravidar e nunca tiveste filhos, mas vais conceber e dar à luz um filho.
pt.R: O anjo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} apareceu à mulher. Ele disse a ela: "Tu não tens conseguido ter filhos. Mas vais ficar grávida e ter um filho.

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: a messenger from the LORD who carries the LORD's own presence
alternatives: the LORD himself in human form
decisions.reason: The word translated "angel" means "messenger". As in 2:1 and 6:11-22, the angel of the LORD is told apart from the LORD and yet is spoken of as if meeting him were meeting God. In this chapter the woman takes him for a "man of God" (verse 6), Manoah does not know who he is (verse 16), and only when he goes up in the flame do they know, and then Manoah says, "We have seen God" (verses 21-22). He may be a heavenly messenger who stands for God so fully that to see him is to see God, or an appearance of the LORD himself. The text does not settle which.

decisions.choice: you will conceive and bear a son: a birth announced by God
decisions.reason: The words follow the pattern of other promised births: to Hagar (Genesis 16:11), to Sarah (Genesis 18:10-14), and later in Isaiah 7:14. A birth announced in this way marks the child as one with a part in God's plan.

decisions.choice: see now: a call to pay attention to what follows
decisions.reason: The first word points to what is about to be said, and the small word after it softens it, like "please". The angel begins with the woman's grief, then turns it around.

decisions.choice: the angel; he, him, his (no capitals for the angel)
decisions.reason: "The angel of the LORD" is kept at every level, as in 2:1 and 6:11. Pronouns for the angel take no capital in any setting, since the narrator speaks of him as the LORD's messenger; where he speaks God's own words in the first person, as in 2:1, those words are treated as God's.

decisions.choice: "malaika wa BWANA" at every level, with ordinary small letters for the angel's pronouns
decisions.reason: As agreed for Judges in every language. Swahili marks the angel inside the verb ("akamwambia"), so the question of capitals for him does not arise; his identity is the subject of the meaning decision (m1).

decisions.choice: "el ángel del SEÑOR", with "él" and "su" for the angel, never capitalised
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: "el ángel del SEÑOR" at every level. The angel carries the LORD's presence (m1), but the pronouns for him follow the English, which gives him no deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "l'ange du SEIGNEUR"; "il", "lui" without the deity pronoun setting for the angel

decisions.choice: "Thiên sứ của CHÚA" at every level; the angel calls the woman "bà"; the narrative calls him "thiên sứ" or "người", never "Ngài"
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note; the English gives the angel no capital pronoun (rendering decision), so the Vietnamese does not use the pronoun of God for him either. "bà" is the respectful word for a married woman.

decisions.choice: The angel speaks in the plain style (해라체) and is told of without the honorific; Manoah and his wife speak to him in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: As for the angel of the LORD in Genesis: he speaks with the authority of the one who sent him, and the people, who first take him for a man of God, speak up to him. The narrative keeps the honorific for the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: o anjo do SENHOR; tu (the angel to the woman and to Manoah)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "o anjo" in lowercase, as Genesis 16:7 and Judges' earlier chapters have it, and pronouns for him take no setting span, as in the English (r-en-1). He speaks with God's voice, so he says "tu" to the woman, as the angel speaks to Hagar in Genesis 16 and as God speaks to one person (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4).

decisions.choice: wine or strong drink: every drink that can make a person drunk

decisions.choice: anything unclean: food the law forbids
decisions.reason: Unclean food is what the law of Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14 forbids, and anything made unclean by contact with the dead (Numbers 6:6-7). Every Israelite was to avoid such food; for her the command is stressed because the child she carries is to be set apart to God.

decisions.choice: beer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "beer" for "strong drink", as in Numbers 6:3.

decisions.choice: "boisson forte" (L); "boisson fermentée" (B, R)
alternatives: "bière", as the English Balanced and Readable "beer"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names any intoxicating drink other than wine (m1). "Bière" would point French readers to one drink only; "boisson fermentée" says what it is. Literal keeps the traditional "boisson forte". The same words are used in 13:7 and 13:14.

decisions.choice: "rượu mạnh" (L), "thức uống có men" (B, R) for *shekhar*
decisions.reason: The word covers every drink that makes a person drunk besides wine (meaning decision). Vietnamese "rượu mạnh" today means spirits, which ancient Israel did not distil, so Balanced and Readable describe it; Literal keeps the traditional word.

decisions.choice: vinho nem bebida forte (L); vinho nem cerveja (B, R)

decisions.choice: a Nazirite of God: one set apart to God
decisions.reason: "Nazirite" means one set apart (Numbers 6:2). Numbers 6 gives the law for a man or woman who chooses to take the vow for a time. Samson is different: God chooses him before birth, and he is to be a Nazirite for life, "until the day of his death" (verse 7). Samuel was given to God in the same way from birth (1 Samuel 1:11).

decisions.choice: no razor on his head: the long hair is the sign of the vow
decisions.reason: Uncut hair was the sign everyone could see that a person was set apart (Numbers 6:5). Samson's strength will be tied to this sign (16:17).

decisions.choice: you are pregnant: the conception is announced as good as done
decisions.reason: The word is an adjective, "pregnant", not a verb. With the pointing word before it, it can mean that she is already pregnant or that she is about to be; the same words are said to Hagar (Genesis 16:11) and in Isaiah 7:14. Verse 3 has just said "you will conceive", so the sense here is the near future.

decisions.choice: he will begin to save Israel: the rescue will not be complete
decisions.reason: Unlike the earlier judges, Samson will only begin the rescue. The Philistines are still a threat at his death and through the days of Samuel and Saul (1 Samuel 7:13; 13:19-22); David is the one who breaks their power (2 Samuel 5:17-25; 8:1).

decisions.choice: a Nazirite, set apart to God (Balanced); a Nazirite ... set apart for God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "Nazirite of God". Balanced and Readable say what the title means, as Numbers 6:2 does at Readable.

decisions.choice: Never cut his hair; from before he is born
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a razor going up on his head and "from the womb" mean.

decisions.choice: "Mnadhiri" for the Nazirite, with "aliyetengwa kwa ajili ya Mungu" (set apart for God) added at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As agreed for these books in every language. The term takes the person prefix m- (plural "Wanadhiri"); Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does, since the word alone is unfamiliar.

decisions.choice: "nazareo"; "consagrado a Dios" (B), "apartado para Dios" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: "nazareo" is the Spanish word for one under the vow of Numbers 6. Balanced and Readable add what it means (m1), as the English does. It is not "nazareno", a man from Nazareth.

decisions.choice: "nazir"; "consacré à Dieu" (B); "mis à part pour Dieu" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books sets: "nazir", the French word for a person under the vow of Numbers 6, and the Hebrew word for "one set apart". Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "người Na-xi-rê" at every level; Balanced and Readable add "được biệt riêng cho Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note; the explanation is the meaning decision's "one set apart to God", added where the English adds it.

decisions.choice: "나실인" at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set. Balanced and Readable add "하나님께 구별된" (set apart to God), which is what the word means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: nazireu de Deus (L); nazireu, separado para Deus (B, R); desde o ventre (L, B), desde antes de nascer (R)
decisions.reason: "Nazireu" is the title Numbers 6:2 uses in Portuguese, and "separado" keeps that chapter's verb for being set apart (m1), as Balanced and Readable explain the title, following the English. "Desde o ventre" is the plain Portuguese for "from the womb"; Readable says what it means. The same wording returns in verse 7 and 16:17.

ko.B: 그 여자가 남편에게 가서 말했다. "하나님의 사람이 저에게 왔어요. 그 모습이 하나님의 천사 같아서 몹시 두려웠어요. 저는 그분이 어디에서 왔는지 묻지 않았고, 그분도 자기 이름을 말해 주지 않았어요.
ko.R: 그 여자가 남편에게 가서 말했다. "하나님의 사람이 저에게 왔어요. 그분은 하나님의 천사처럼 보였고, 저는 무서웠어요. 저는 그분에게 어디에서 왔느냐고 묻지 않았고, 그분도 이름을 말해 주지 않았어요.

pt.L: E a mulher veio e falou ao seu marido, dizendo: "Um homem de Deus veio a mim, e a sua aparência [era] como a aparência do anjo de Deus, muito temível; e eu não lhe perguntei de onde ele [era], e ele não me disse o seu nome.
pt.B: A mulher foi até o marido e disse: "Um homem de Deus veio a mim. Ele parecia o anjo de Deus, de causar temor. Eu não perguntei de onde ele era, e ele não me disse o seu nome.
pt.R: A mulher foi até o marido e contou: "Um homem de Deus veio falar comigo. Ele parecia um anjo de Deus, e eu fiquei com medo. Eu não perguntei de onde ele era, e ele não disse qual era o seu nome.

decisions.choice: a man of God: a prophet, one who speaks for God
decisions.reason: The title is used of Moses (Deuteronomy 33:1) and of prophets (1 Samuel 2:27; 9:6). The woman thinks a human prophet has come to her; she does not yet know who he is.

decisions.choice: like the angel of God, very awesome: his look filled her with fear and wonder
decisions.reason: The word means one who causes fear or awe. Something in his appearance made her think he was more than a man, though she cannot say what. Whether she means one particular angel or what any angel would look like is not clear; the Hebrew phrase can be read either way.

decisions.choice: she did not ask where he came from, and he did not tell his name
decisions.reason: Asking a visitor's home and name was ordinary courtesy. The angel's name becomes the question of verses 17-18.

decisions.choice: he made me afraid
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "very awesome" in plain words, with the fear that the word carries.

decisions.choice: Manoah's wife says "em" to her husband, and he says "em" to her and "anh" for himself
decisions.reason: As the Genesis note sets for husband and wife; used at every level here, since the English Literal keeps no special formality between them.

decisions.choice: Manoah and his wife speak to each other in the polite informal style (해요체)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for husband and wife.

decisions.choice: muito temível (L); de causar temor (B)
decisions.reason: The word is one who causes fear and awe (m2). "Temível" and "temor" keep the fear in it; "terrível" in Brazilian usage means only "very bad", and "impressionante" loses the fear that the English Readable keeps.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ הָרָ֖ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֑ן וְעַתָּ֞ה אַל־תִּשְׁתִּ֣י׀יַ֣יִן וְשֵׁכָ֗ר וְאַל־תֹּֽאכְלִי֙ כָּל־טֻמְאָ֔ה כִּֽי־נְזִ֤יר אֱלֹהִים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַנַּ֔עַר מִן־הַבֶּ֖טֶן עַד־י֥וֹם מוֹתֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, see, you [will be] pregnant and will bear [a] son; and now, do not drink wine and strong drink, and do not eat any uncleanness, for [a] Nazirite of God will be the boy from the womb until [the] day of his death.

en.L: And he said to me, 'See, you [will be] pregnant and will bear a son; and now, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.'"
en.B: But he said to me, 'You will conceive and give birth to a son. So now, drink no wine or beer, and eat nothing unclean, for the boy is to be a Nazirite, set apart to God from the womb until the day he dies.'"
en.R: But he told me, 'You will become pregnant and have a son. So do not drink wine or beer, and do not eat any food that is unclean. The boy will be a Nazirite, set apart for God from before he is born until the day he dies.'"

sw.L: Naye akaniambia, 'Tazama, utachukua mimba na kuzaa mwana; basi sasa usinywe divai wala kileo, wala usile kitu chochote kilicho najisi, kwa maana kijana atakuwa Mnadhiri wa Mungu tangu tumboni mpaka siku ya kufa kwake.'"
sw.B: Lakini aliniambia, 'Utachukua mimba na kuzaa mwana. Basi sasa usinywe divai wala pombe, wala usile kitu chochote kilicho najisi, kwa sababu kijana huyo atakuwa Mnadhiri, aliyetengwa kwa ajili ya Mungu tangu tumboni mpaka siku atakapokufa.'"
sw.R: Lakini aliniambia, 'Utapata mimba na kuzaa mtoto wa kiume. Kwa hiyo usinywe divai wala pombe, wala usile chakula chochote kilicho najisi. Mtoto huyo atakuwa Mnadhiri, aliyetengwa kwa ajili ya Mungu tangu kabla hajazaliwa mpaka siku atakapokufa.'"

es.L: Y me dijo: “He aquí, [estás] encinta y darás a luz un hijo; y ahora, no bebas vino ni bebida fuerte, y no comas nada impuro, porque nazareo de Dios será el niño desde el vientre hasta el día de su muerte”».
es.B: Pero me dijo: “Concebirás y darás a luz un hijo. Así que ahora no bebas vino ni cerveza, y no comas nada impuro, porque el niño será nazareo, consagrado a Dios desde el vientre hasta el día de su muerte”».
es.R: Pero me dijo: “Vas a quedar embarazada y tendrás un hijo. Así que no bebas vino ni cerveza, y no comas ningún alimento impuro. El niño será nazareo, apartado para Dios desde antes de nacer hasta el día en que muera”».

fr.L: Et il m’a dit : “Voici, tu [seras] enceinte et tu enfanteras un fils ; et maintenant, ne bois pas de vin ni de boisson forte, et ne mange rien d’impur, car l’enfant sera nazir de Dieu dès le ventre jusqu’au jour de sa mort.” »
fr.B: Mais il m’a dit : “Tu vas concevoir et mettre au monde un fils. Maintenant donc, ne bois ni vin ni boisson fermentée, et ne mange rien d’impur, car l’enfant sera nazir, consacré à Dieu dès le ventre de sa mère jusqu’au jour de sa mort.” »
fr.R: Mais il m’a dit : “Tu vas être enceinte et tu auras un fils. Alors ne bois pas de vin ni de boisson fermentée, et ne mange aucun aliment impur. L’enfant sera nazir, mis à part pour Dieu avant sa naissance et jusqu’au jour de sa mort.” »

vi.L: Người nói với em: 'Này, bà [sẽ] có thai và sinh một con trai; vậy bây giờ, đừng uống rượu nho hay rượu mạnh, và đừng ăn gì ô uế, vì đứa trẻ sẽ là người Na-xi-rê của Đức Chúa Trời từ trong lòng mẹ cho đến ngày nó qua đời.'"
vi.B: Nhưng người bảo em: 'Bà sẽ thụ thai và sinh một con trai. Vậy bây giờ, đừng uống rượu nho hay thức uống có men, và đừng ăn bất cứ thứ gì ô uế, vì đứa trẻ sẽ là người Na-xi-rê, được biệt riêng cho Đức Chúa Trời từ trong lòng mẹ cho đến ngày qua đời.'"
vi.R: Nhưng người bảo em: 'Bà sẽ có thai và sinh một con trai. Vậy đừng uống rượu nho hay thức uống có men, và đừng ăn bất cứ thức ăn nào ô uế. Đứa trẻ sẽ là người Na-xi-rê, được biệt riêng cho Đức Chúa Trời từ trước khi sinh ra cho đến ngày qua đời.'"

ko.L: 그런데 그가 저에게 말했어요. '보아라, 너는 임신하여 아들을 낳을 것이다. 그러니 이제 포도주나 독한 술을 마시지 말고, 부정한 것은 아무것도 먹지 마라. 그 아이는 모태에서부터 죽는 날까지 하나님의 나실인이 될 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그분이 저에게 말했어요. '너는 임신하여 아들을 낳을 것이다. 그러니 이제 포도주나 독한 술을 마시지 말고, 부정한 것은 아무것도 먹지 마라. 그 아이는 모태에서부터 죽는 날까지 하나님께 구별된 나실인이 될 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그분이 저에게 이렇게 말했어요. '너는 아이를 가져서 아들을 낳을 것이다. 그러니 포도주나 맥주 같은 술을 마시지 말고, 부정한 음식은 아무것도 먹지 마라. 그 아이는 나실인이 될 것이다. 태어나기 전부터 죽는 날까지 하나님께 구별된 사람이 될 것이다.'"

pt.L: E ele me disse: 'Eis que [estarás] grávida e darás à luz um filho; e agora, não bebas vinho nem bebida forte, e não comas nada impuro, pois o menino será nazireu de Deus desde o ventre até o dia da sua morte.'"
pt.B: Mas ele me disse: 'Vais conceber e dar à luz um filho. Portanto, não bebas vinho nem cerveja, e não comas nada impuro, porque o menino será nazireu, separado para Deus desde o ventre até o dia da sua morte.'"
pt.R: Mas ele me disse: 'Tu vais ficar grávida e ter um filho. Por isso não bebas vinho nem cerveja, e não comas nenhum alimento impuro. O menino vai ser nazireu, separado para Deus desde antes de nascer até o dia em que morrer.'"

decisions.choice: until the day of his death: what the woman adds
decisions.reason: The woman repeats the angel's words, with two changes. She leaves out the razor and the promise that her son will begin to save Israel, and she adds "until the day of his death". The added words look ahead to how the story ends: Samson keeps the Nazirite sign until it is cut, and he dies among the Philistines (16:30).

decisions.choice: anything unclean: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The noun here means "uncleanness" where verse 4 has the adjective; the sense is the same, food the law forbids.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside the woman's words
decisions.reason: The woman quotes the angel, so his words stand inside her speech.

decisions.choice: tu inside the quotation; você between the woman and Manoah
decisions.reason: The woman repeats the angel's words as he said them, so they keep his "tu" ("darás", "não bebas") inside the single quotation marks, while she herself speaks to her husband in the plain first person; her words to Manoah elsewhere take "você", the form between people.

source.text: וַיֶּעְתַּ֥ר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בִּ֣י אֲדוֹנָ֔י אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֞ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֗חְתָּ יָבוֹא־נָ֥א עוֹד֙ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְיוֹרֵ֕נוּ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַנַּ֥עַר הַיּוּלָּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And prayed Manoah to Yahweh and said, please, my Lord, [the] man of God whom you sent, let him come please again to us, and let him teach us what we shall do for the boy who will be born.

en.L: And Manoah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Please, my Lord, let the man of God whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent come again to us, please, and let him teach us what we shall do for the boy who will be born."
en.B: Then Manoah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "Please, my Lord, let the man of God whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent come to us again and teach us what we should do for the boy who is to be born."
en.R: Then Manoah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "Lord, please let the man of God {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent come to us again. Let him teach us how we should raise the boy who is going to be born."

sw.L: Naye Manoa akamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Tafadhali, Bwana wangu, yule mtu wa Mungu uliyemtuma na aje tena kwetu, tafadhali, atufundishe tutakalomfanyia kijana atakayezaliwa."
sw.B: Kisha Manoa alimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: "Tafadhali, Bwana wangu, yule mtu wa Mungu uliyemtuma na aje kwetu tena atufundishe tunachopaswa kumfanyia kijana atakayezaliwa."
sw.R: Kisha Manoa alimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Alisema, "Bwana, tafadhali mruhusu yule mtu wa Mungu uliyemtuma aje kwetu tena. Atufundishe jinsi tunavyopaswa kumlea mtoto atakayezaliwa."

es.L: Y Manoa oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «Te ruego, Señor mío, que el hombre de Dios que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} enviaste venga otra vez, te ruego, a nosotros, y nos enseñe qué hemos de hacer con el niño que ha de nacer».
es.B: Entonces Manoa oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «Te ruego, Señor mío, que el hombre de Dios que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} enviaste vuelva a nosotros y nos enseñe qué debemos hacer con el niño que va a nacer».
es.R: Entonces Manoa oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Le dijo: «Señor, por favor, deja que el hombre de Dios que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} enviaste vuelva a visitarnos. Que nos enseñe cómo debemos criar al niño que va a nacer».

fr.L: Et Manoah pria {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et dit : « Je t’en prie, mon Seigneur, que l’homme de Dieu que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé vienne encore vers nous, je te prie, et qu’il nous enseigne ce que nous ferons pour l’enfant qui naîtra. »
fr.B: Alors Manoah pria {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « Je t’en prie, mon Seigneur, que l’homme de Dieu que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé revienne vers nous et nous enseigne ce que nous devrons faire pour l’enfant qui va naître. »
fr.R: Alors Manoah a prié {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Il a dit : « Seigneur, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, laisse revenir vers nous l’homme de Dieu que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as envoyé. Qu’il nous apprenne comment nous devons élever l’enfant qui va naître. »

vi.L: Ma-nô-a cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nói: "Lạy Chúa, xin cho người của Đức Chúa Trời mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai trở lại với chúng con một lần nữa, và dạy chúng con điều phải làm cho đứa trẻ sẽ được sinh ra."
vi.B: Bấy giờ Ma-nô-a cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Lạy Chúa, xin cho người của Đức Chúa Trời mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai trở lại với chúng con một lần nữa, để dạy chúng con phải làm gì cho đứa trẻ sắp được sinh ra."
vi.R: Bấy giờ Ma-nô-a cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông nói: "Lạy Chúa, xin cho người của Đức Chúa Trời mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã sai đến trở lại với chúng con. Xin cho người dạy chúng con phải nuôi dạy đứa trẻ sắp sinh ra như thế nào."

ko.L: 마노아가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도하여 말했다. "제 주님, 부디 주께서 보내신 하나님의 사람을 우리에게 다시 오게 하셔서, 태어날 아이에게 우리가 어떻게 해야 할지 가르치게 해 주십시오."
ko.B: 그러자 마노아가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도했다. "제 주님, 부디 주께서 보내신 하나님의 사람을 우리에게 다시 보내 주셔서, 태어날 아이를 위해 우리가 무엇을 해야 할지 가르쳐 주게 하십시오."
ko.R: 그러자 마노아가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 기도했다. 그가 말했다. "주님, 주께서 보내신 하나님의 사람을 우리에게 다시 보내 주십시오. 그래서 태어날 아이를 어떻게 길러야 할지 우리에게 가르쳐 주게 하십시오."

pt.L: E Manoá orou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e disse: "Por favor, meu Senhor, que o homem de Deus que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enviaste venha outra vez a nós, por favor, e nos ensine o que devemos fazer com o menino que vai nascer."
pt.B: Então Manoá orou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Por favor, meu Senhor, permite que o homem de Deus que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enviaste venha de novo até nós e nos ensine o que devemos fazer com o menino que vai nascer."
pt.R: Então Manoá orou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Ele disse: "Senhor, por favor, deixa que o homem de Deus que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enviaste venha de novo até nós. Que ele nos ensine como devemos criar o menino que vai nascer."

decisions.choice: please, my Lord: a humble plea addressed to God
decisions.reason: The first word asks for a hearing, "please" or "pardon me". The title "my Lord" here has the form used only for God, and Manoah speaks it in a prayer to the LORD, as Gideon does in 6:15.

decisions.choice: Manoah believes the message and asks for more
decisions.reason: Manoah does not doubt what his wife has told him. He accepts that the man was sent by God and asks only how they are to bring up the child.

decisions.choice: the boy who will be born: a child not yet conceived
decisions.reason: The verb form describes what is still to come. The child has been promised but not yet conceived (verse 24).

decisions.choice: how we should raise the boy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "what we shall do for the boy" is about: how to bring him up.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa" for "please, my Lord" (*Adonai*)
decisions.reason: Adonai is "Chúa", never in capitals, as the Genesis note sets; "Lạy" is the Vietnamese word of humble address in prayer, which carries the Hebrew "please".

decisions.choice: "제 주님" for Adonai, "my Lord"
decisions.reason: Manoah speaks to God; Adonai is "주님", as the Korean Old Testament renders it, and he prays in the formal polite style.

decisions.choice: meu Senhor, with tu ("tu enviaste", "permite", "deixa")
decisions.reason: Manoah prays to the LORD, so he says "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), and the title has a capital, "Senhor", as for Adonai in the terms doc (m1). The pronoun "tu" is kept before "enviaste" to carry the setting span the English has on "you".
